h: David HaMelech’s prayer joins supplication for true salvation with the discipline of blessing and adversity.
What to Request During an Auspicious Time

p: וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה' עֵת רָצוֹן".
"'And as for me, may my prayer come to You, Hashem, at an acceptable time.'
הוֹרָה לָנוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
King David, peace be upon him, instructed us:
כְּשֶׁנִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעֵת רָצוֹן, עַל מַה נִּתְפַּלֵּל?
when we pray during an acceptable time, for what should we pray?
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַתְּפִלָּה: "אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב חַסְדֶּךָ",
That the prayer be: 'O God, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness,'
שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁנּוּכַל לִפְעוֹל רַב חֶסֶד בְּעֵת רָצוֹן,
for since we can effect abundant lovingkindness during an acceptable time,
מְבַקְּשִׁים אָנוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּרוֹב הַחֶסֶד שֶׁיַּשְׁפִּיעַ לָנוּ
we beseech that within the abundance of kindness He bestows upon us
גַּם מִדַּת צִמְצוּם,
there be also the attribute of containment/restraint (tsimtsum),
שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים, פַּחַד יִצְחָק.
which is denoted by the Name Elohim, the Awe of Isaac.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק הַחֶסֶד לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Namely, that the lovingkindness should not impair one's service of Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
just as King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed: "
רֵישׁ וָעֹשֶׁר אַל תִּתֶּן לִי, פֶּן אֶשְׂבַּע וְכִחַשְׁתִּי".
"'Poverty and wealth give me not, lest I be sated and deny.'
וְכֵן הוֹרוּ לָנוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כה:):
And so our Sages of blessed memory instructed us (Bava Batra 25b): "
הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּעֲשִׁיר – יַצְפִּין",
"He who desires to become wealthy, let him turn north,"
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁרוֹצֶה בְּעוֹשֶׁר
for one who desires wealth
וְשֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק לוֹ הָעוֹשֶׁר לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that this wealth should not compromise his service of Hashem, blessed be He,
יַחֲזִיק בְּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה, פַּחַד יִצְחָק;
must hold fast to the attribute of reverence, the Awe of Isaac;
וְזֶהוּ "יַצְפִּין" – צַד צָפוֹן, בְּחִינַת גְּבוּרָה,
and this is 'let him turn north'—the northern direction, the dimension of Gevurah, "
וּמִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶאֱתֶה".
'and from the north comes gold.' "
עֲנֵנִי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׁעֶךָ"
– 'Answer me in the truth of Your salvation'—
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַיְשׁוּעָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ אֱמֶת,
that the salvation be established upon the path of truth, "
וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד",
and 'the lip of truth shall be established forever,'
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעָלְמֵי עַד, לְעוֹלָם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ אָרוֹךְ.
that it endure for eternal worlds, for the World that is entirely boundless.
אֲבָל כָּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דְּבַר אֱמֶת
– However, whatever lacks the quality of truth— "
עַד אַרְגִּיעָה לְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר",
'a false tongue is but for a moment,'
כִּי כָּל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא "עַד אַרְגִּיעָה".
for all transient life of this world is termed 'for a moment.'
וְלָכֵן אוֹמְרִים פָּסוּק זֶה בְּמִנְחָה בְּשַׁבָּת,
Therefore we recite this verse during Minchah on Shabbat,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דְּרַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין אִשְׁתְּכַח בֵּיהּ,
for it is taught in the holy Zohar that the Will of all Wills (Ra'ava de-Ra'avin) is present then,
וִיכוֹלִין לִפְעוֹל כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת, רַב חֶסֶד.
and one can effect all divine goodness, abundant lovingkindness.
וְעַל זֶה אָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין: "אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב חַסְדֶּךָ" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
And upon this we plead: 'O God, in the abundance of Your lovingkindness,' as noted above.
וּבִבְרָכוֹת כְּתִיב: "וּבָאוּ עָלֶיךָ כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְהִשִּׂיגֻךָ",
And regarding the blessings it is written: 'And all these blessings shall come upon you, and overtake you,'
וְאוֹמְרִים בְּשֵׁם רַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי בִּינֶם זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
and they cite in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim, of blessed memory for the World to Come: "
וְהִשִּׂיגוּךָ בִּמְקוֹמְךָ",
'and they shall overtake you in your place,'
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתַּנֶּה עַל יְדֵי הַטּוֹבוֹת וְהַחֲסָדִים וְהַבְּרָכוֹת;
meaning that you not be altered through the bounties, kindnesses, and blessings;
וְהוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה "אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב חַסְדֶּךָ",
and this is that there be 'Elohim in the abundance of Your kindness,'
שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכְּחוּ כִּי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ הַנֹּתֵן לְךָ כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חָיִל.
that they forget not that it is Hashem your God Who gives you strength to acquire wealth.
וְכֵן מִתְפַּלְּלִין בִּצְלוֹתָא דְּרַב
And so we pray in the supplication of Rav
אַחַר עֶשֶׂר לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל חַיִּים:
following the ten expressions of life: "
חַיִּים שֶׁתְּמַלֵּא לָנוּ אֶת כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבֵּנוּ לְטוֹבָה",
'a life wherein You fulfill all our hearts' desires for good,'
שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בַּמִּדְבָּר פָּרָשָׁה א):
for so we find in Midrash Rabbah (Bemidbar, Parashah 1):
שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין אוֹמֵר כֵּן,
that regarding Israel Scripture speaks conditionally,
רַק "כְּכָל דְּרָכָיו אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַע אֶת לְבָבוֹ",
saying 'according to all his ways, whose heart You know,'
אִם הָיָה רָאוּי לוֹ הָיָה נוֹתֵן לוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
that if it were fitting for him, He would grant it to him, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק לוֹ הַטּוֹבָה שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ.
And this signifies likewise that the bounty he requests should not harm him.
וּבְשַׁבָּת מָצִינוּ (שַׁבָּת קיח:):
And on Shabbat we find (Shabbat 118b):
בַּמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ,
regarding one who delights in Shabbat, that they give him the desires of his heart,
וְלֹא נֶזְכַּר "לְטוֹבָה".
and 'for good' is not appended.
וְהַטַּעַם: שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת כָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְבַקֵּשׁ הוּא הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה
And the reason is: on Shabbat, everything a Jew requests is inherently for good,
וְלֹא יַזִּיק לוֹ.
and will not harm him.
וְזֶה דְּאִיתָא (תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ):
And this clarifies what is brought (Tanchuma, this parashah):
דְּאֵין מִתְעַנִּין בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
that one does not fast on Friday,
דִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת עָדִיף מֵאֶלֶף תַּעֲנִיּוֹת;
for the honor of Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts;
דִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְתַעֲנִית דְּרַבָּנָן,
because honoring Shabbat is biblical while a fast is rabbinic,
וְאָתֵי כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת וְדָחֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and honoring Shabbat comes and overrides it, see there.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה טַעַם הַשֵּׁנִי מַסְפִּיק,
And seemingly the second rationale is sufficient,
שֶׁכְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דָּחֵי תַּעֲנִית דְּרַבָּנָן.
that biblical honor of Shabbat overrides a rabbinic fast.
אַךְ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִקְדִּים דְּעִיקַּר תַּעֲנִית סְלִיחוֹת וְרַחֲמִים הוּא,
However, because he prefaced that the core purpose of a fast is forgiveness and mercy,
וְאָתֵי לְאִמָּנוּעֵי מִכְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת,
and he might come to withhold from honoring Shabbat,
וְאִם כֵּן מַה מוֹעִיל דִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
and if so, what does it avail that Shabbat honor is biblical,
הָא בָּעֵינַן סְלִיחוֹת וְרַחֲמִים?
when we still require forgiveness and mercy?
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת עָדִיף מֵאֶלֶף תַּעֲנִיּוֹת,
And to this he stated that honoring Shabbat surpasses a thousand fasts,
וְעַל יְדֵי כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ
and through honoring Shabbat he can attain all the desires of his heart,
וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה,
and that everything will be for the good,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ עוֹד לִסְלִיחוֹת וְרַחֲמִים,
and he no longer requires penitential fasts and pleas for mercy;
וְלָמָּה לֵיהּ לְאִמָּנוּעֵי מִכְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
why then should he withhold from the biblical honor of Shabbat?
וּמִמֵּילָא אָתֵי כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְדָחֵי תַּעֲנִית דְּרַבָּנָן.
and automatically biblical honor of Shabbat comes and overrides the rabbinic fast.
וּבְהֵיפֶךְ, בַּתּוֹכָחוֹת כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן "וְהִשִּׂיגֻךָ",
And conversely, in the admonitions it is likewise written 'and shall overtake you,'
וְנִרְאֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַנִּזְכָּר:
and it appears also in the aforementioned manner:
שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה,
that he should not be displaced from his spiritual standing through it,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (עֵירוּבִין מא:):
along the lines of what is stated (Eruvin 41b):
שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הַמַּעֲבִירִין אֶת הָאָדָם עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ.
that there are three things that turn a person away from the mindset of his Creator.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹלֵחַ יִסּוּרִין רַק לְטוֹבָתֵנוּ,
And since Hashem sends afflictions solely for our ultimate benefit,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ וְגוֹמֵר",
as is stated: 'As a man chastens his son, etc.',
אֵינוֹ שׁוֹלֵחַ יִסּוּרִין שֶׁיַּעֲבִירוּ אוֹתוֹ עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ,
He does not send afflictions that would turn him away from the mindset of his Creator,
רַק שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַיִּסּוּרִין יִזְכֶּה לְחַיֵּי עַד,
rather that through the afflictions he should merit eternal life,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְדֶרֶךְ חַיִּים תּוֹכְחוֹת מוּסָר" (עַיֵּין בְּרָכוֹת ה:).
as is stated: 'and reproofs of instruction are the way of life' (see Berakhot 5a).
וְכֵן "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי".
And likewise: 'Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.'

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 25b: ‘Rabbi Yitzḥak says: One who wishes to become wise should face south, and one who wishes to become wealthy should face north. And your mnemonic for this is that in the Temple the Table, which symbolized blessing and abundance, was in the north, and the Candelabrum, which symbolized the light of wisdom, was in the south of the Sanctuary. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: One should always face south, as once he becomes wise he will subsequently also become wealthy, as it is stated with regard to the Torah: “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor” (Proverbs 3:16).’

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (בַּמִּדְבָּר פָּרָשָׁה א):
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: for so we find in Midrash Rabbah (Bemidbar, Parashah 1):

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 1:3: “Another matter: “The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai” – Before the Tent of Meeting stood, He spoke with him at the bush, as it is stated: “God called to him from within the bush” (Exodus 3:4). Then, “God said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying.” (Exodus 12:1) He spoke with him in Midian, as it is stated: “The Lord spoke to Moses in Midian” (Exodus 4:19). He spoke to him in Sinai, as it is stated: “The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai…saying.” Once the Tent of Meeting stood, He said: Modesty [tzeniut] is preferable, as it is stated: “And to walk humbly [hatzne’a] with your God” (Micah 6:8) – He speaks with him in the Tent of Meeting. Likewise, David said: “All of the glory of a king’s daughter is within, her dress interwoven with gold” (Psalms 45:14). “A king’s daughter” – this is Moses, as it is stated: “I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a harsh master” (Isaiah 19:4) – these are the plagues that came upon Egypt. “And a strong [oz] king will rule over them” (Isaiah 19:4) – this is Moses, who was the king of the Torah, which is called oz, as it is stated: “The Lord will give strength [oz] to His people” (Psalms 29:11). Therefore, “all of the glory of a king’s daughter is within.” “[All of the glory [kevudah] of a king’s daughter is within,] her dress interwoven [mimishbetzot] with gold” – this is Aaron, as it is stated: “You shall make settings [mishbetzot] of gold” (Exodus 28:13). From here they said: A woman who conducts herself modestly, even if she is an Israelite, is worthy to marry a priest and to produce High Priests, as it is stated: “Her dress interwoven [mimishbetzot] with gold.” The Holy One blessed be He said: This is My honor [kavod], that I will speak within. As it is stated: “When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting [to speak with Him]” (Numbers 7:89). Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: If the nations of the world would know how much the Temple benefited them, they would have surrounded it with fortifications to protect it, as it was more beneficial for them than it was for Israel, as Solomon prayed: “To the foreigner, as well, who is not of Your people Israel” (I Kings 8:41), and it is written: “You will act in accordance with everything that the foreigner calls to You” (I Kings 8:43). But when he comes to Israel, what is written? “May You grant to each man according to all his ways, as you know his heart” (II Chronicles 6:30) – if he was worthy of it, He would give to him; if not, He would not give to him. Do not say: The Temple [alone benefits all nations]; rather, were it not for Israel, rain would not fall, the sun would not shine, as it is due to their merit that the Holy One blessed be He brings wellbeing to the world. rich.text: : “Another matter: “The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai” – Before the Tent of Meeting stood, He spoke with him at the bush, as it is stated: “God called to him from within the bush” (Exodus 3:4). He spoke to him in Sinai, as it is stated: “The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai…saying.” Once the Tent of Meeting stood, He said: Modesty [tzeniut] is preferable, as it is stated: “And to walk humbly [hatzne’a] with your God” (Micah 6:8) – He speaks with him in the Tent of Meeting. Likewise, David said: “All of the glory of a king’s daughter is within, her dress interwoven with gold” (Psalms 45:14). “A king’s daughter” – this is Moses, as it is stated: “I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a harsh master” (Isaiah 19:4) – these are the plagues that came upon Egypt. “And a strong [oz] king will rule over them” (Isaiah 19:4) – this is Moses, who was the king of the Torah, which is called oz, as it is stated: “The Lord will give strength [oz] to His people” (Psalms 29:11). paragraphs.text: Shabbat 118b:2: “Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: One who delights in Shabbat is rescued from the oppression of exile. He derives it by means of a verbal analogy. It is written here, with regard to Shabbat: “And I will cause you to ride on the heights [bamotei] of the world” (Isaiah 58:14), and it is written there: “You are fortunate Israel, who is like you? A nation redeemed by God, the shield that aids you and the sword of your triumph. Your enemies will try to defeat you and you will trample their high places [bamoteimo]” (Deuteronomy 33:29). Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: With regard to anyone who delights in the Shabbat, God grants him his heart’s desires, as it is stated: “And you shall delight in God and He will grant you your heart’s desires” (Psalms 37:4). This delight in God, which is mentioned in the verse, I do not know what it is. When it says: “And you shall call the Shabbat delight,” one must say: It is the delight of Shabbat. The Gemara asks: With what does one delight in the day of Shabbat? Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: With a dish of beets, and large fish, and heads of garlic. Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said: Even with regard to a small item and one prepared it in deference to Shabbat, it is a delight. The Gemara asks: What is the small item mentioned? Rav Pappa said: Small fried fish.”

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And this clarifies what is brought (Tanchuma, this parashah):

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Bereshit 3:9: “If the fourteenth falls on Shabbos, it is forbidden to fast on Friday because of the work of preparing for Shabbos. The essence of the fast is prayers for forgiveness and mercy, and it could prevent honoring Shabbos. Honoring Shabbos is preferable to a thousand fasts, for Shabbos honor is a Torah obligation, whereas the fast is rabbinic; the Torah obligation of honoring Shabbos comes and overrides the rabbinic fast.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 215:1: “The heart is the receiving vessel, as Shabbat 31a says that awe is the storehouse, and Yoma 72b, on “but he has no heart,” locates awe there. Fear of Heaven means setting a boundary to the inclination’s craving within the heart; this is within a person’s control. In proportion to the heart’s purity from every kind of refuse, it becomes a greater vessel for goodness and blessing. Above all, it must be clean of pride and envy: this is the essential receiving vessel, so that abundant good will not produce pride, which draws envy, hatred and the other bad qualities after it. Therefore peace is the vessel that holds blessing. Prayer, in which a person asks the blessed God for good, concludes with it: at the end he asks for peace so that he may be a receiving vessel for abundant good.”
